title: EvoGround: Self-Evolving Video Agents for Video Temporal Grounding

problems.name: Annotation Scarcity and Noisy Supervision
problems.evidence_sentence: Trained on 2.5K unlabeled videos, EvoGround matches or surpasses fully supervised models across multiple VTG benchmarks, while emerging as a state-of-the-art fine-grained video captioner without manual labels. # Abstract Video temporal grounding (VTG) takes an untrimmed video and a natural-language query as input and localizes the temporal moment that best matches the query.

problems.name: Dataset, Benchmark, and Evaluation Mismatch
problems.evidence_sentence: We introduce EvoGround, a framework of two coupled self-evolving agents, a proposer and a solver, that learn temporal grounding from raw videos without any human-labeled data.

problems.name: Multi-Moment, Compositional, and Complex Query Grounding
problems.evidence_sentence: We challenge this assumption with EvoGround, a framework of two coupled self-evolving agents that learn to ground temporal moments through mutual interaction without manual labels.

methods.name: LLM Reasoning, Agentic Workflows, or RL Post-Training
methods.evidence_sentence: As shown in Figure 1, EvoGround consists of a proposer and a solver, evolved through an iterative two-stage process via reinforcement learning (RL), with both agents initialized from the same base model.

methods.name: Benchmark or Dataset Construction
methods.evidence_sentence: Despite remarkable progress, existing models typically rely on large-scale human-labeled data for training, fundamentally limiting their scalability and applicability.
